key_insight: A high-order geometry-conforming immersed finite element method achieves optimal error rates on curved domains without requiring the mesh to fit internal interfaces.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports accurate elliptic interface simulations in heterogeneous materials with asymptotically the same global degrees of freedom as standard continuous FEM.
method: Use an outer-boundary-conforming triangular mesh that need not align with the internal interface.
Combine Frenet–Serret-based immersed elements, curved-boundary elements, and standard Lagrange elements.
Apply a symmetric selective discontinuous Galerkin formulation with proven approximation estimates, trace inequalities, and stability.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical O(h^m) energy-norm and O(h^{m+1}) L2-norm convergence rates and demonstrate fewer global degrees of freedom than fully discontinuous Galerkin.
watch_item: Optimal L2 convergence requires standard dual-problem regularity, while implementation must handle interface geometry and curved-boundary elements.
paper_title: A High-Order Geometry-Conforming Selective Discontinuous Galerkin Method and Its Error Analysis for Elliptic Interface Problems on Curved Domains
